registration_checklist: 1. Confirm UNGM Level 1 status is active and up-to-date (UNGM ID 263073) — log in to https://www.ungm.org, verify all Level 1 fields are complete, and note the UNGM confirmation reference number for use in the UNDP eTendering profile.
2. Rename and package all supporting documents using the UN-friendly filename convention defined in document_renaming_rules before uploading anywhere.

3. Navigate to https://procurement-notices.undp.org and click 'Register' to create a new vendor account on the UNDP eTendering portal — use the exact legal company name 'POWERGEN RENEWABLE ENERGY EAST AFRICA LIMITED' as it appears on the Certificate of Incorporation.

4. Complete the UNDP eTendering company profile: enter UNGM ID 263073, legal address (Nairobi HQ), company type (private limited / EPC contractor), year of establishment (2011), headcount (~85), and primary contact details.

5. Select and enter UNSPSC commodity codes in the UNDP eTendering profile — use the codes recommended in organization_profile_notes; choose 5-7 codes that precisely match mini-grid EPC, solar PV installation, O&M services, and renewable energy consulting.
6. Upload the capability statement (tailored UNDP version as drafted in capability_statement_draft) as the primary company profile document.
7. Upload audited financial statements (2022, 2023, 2024 — Deloitte consolidated) and the Equity Bank letter as evidence of financial capacity.
8. Upload ISO 9001 + ISO 45001 certificates, USAID Power Africa reference letter, and AfDB SEFA Project Completion Report as technical and past-performance evidence.
9. Upload the Code of Conduct + Anti-Corruption policy and the Professional Indemnity Insurance Certificate to satisfy UNDP's ethical and risk compliance requirements.

10. Register the UNDP eTendering account for EACH country office where PowerGen operates: Kenya (CO Nairobi), Tanzania (CO Dar es Salaam), Uganda (CO Kampala), Rwanda (CO Kigali), and Ethiopia (CO Addis Ababa) — UNDP procurement is decentralised and country offices issue their own tenders.

11. Use the UNDP eTendering portal's search and filter function to identify active or upcoming tenders in the energy, environment, and infrastructure categories across the five country offices; bookmark relevant tenders.

12. Subscribe to email notifications for tender categories: Energy / Renewable Energy, Environment & Climate, Infrastructure & Construction, and Capacity Building — for Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda, and Ethiopia.

13. Prepare a short bid library folder (capability statement, financials, ISO certs, references, insurance) so that when a 2-3 week RFP/RFQ window opens, documents can be attached immediately without re-formatting.
14. Verify that UNGM Level 1 data (legal name, address, UNSPSC codes) exactly matches the UNDP eTendering profile — discrepancies between the two systems can cause automatic de-listing.
15. Set a 6-month calendar reminder to refresh the UNDP eTendering profile, update audited financials when the 2025 Deloitte audit is complete, and renew ISO certificates before expiry.
output.capability_statement_draft:
POWERGEN RENEWABLE ENERGY EAST AFRICA LIMITED is a pan-African distributed renewable energy developer and EPC contractor headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, with operational offices in Arusha (Tanzania), Kampala (Uganda), and country-level presence in Rwanda and Ethiopia. Founded in 2011 and employing approximately 85 professionals across engineering, project finance, operations, and business development, PowerGen designs, builds, and operates solar PV and battery storage mini-grids, AC/DC microgrids, and solar home system supply chains for rural and peri-urban communities across East Africa. The company has delivered over 60 operational mini-grids serving more than 45,000 households, making it one of the most experienced distributed renewable energy EPC contractors on the continent.

PowerGen's core capabilities are directly aligned with UNDP's energy access, climate action, and sustainable development mandates. The company provides end-to-end project delivery: site identification and feasibility, regulatory licensing and community engagement, solar PV and BESS system design, full EPC execution, low-voltage distribution network construction, and long-term operations and maintenance. PowerGen has successfully executed multi-year grant-funded programmes for USAID Power Africa (2019–2024), the African Development Bank's Sustainable Energy Fund for Africa (2020–2023), and the Shell Foundation, demonstrating the financial management discipline, donor-compliance rigour, and field execution capacity that UNDP country offices require in implementation partners.

Three differentiators set PowerGen apart in the UNDP supplier landscape. First, verified track record at scale: 12 EPC contracts delivered on time with no audit qualifications, independently confirmed by a clean 2024 Deloitte East Africa consolidated audit and a USAID Power Africa reference letter. Second, dual ISO certification: ISO 9001 (quality management) and ISO 45001 (occupational health and safety), ensuring that every project meets international quality and worker-safety standards — a critical requirement for donor-funded rural infrastructure. Third, deep East African regulatory and community knowledge: PowerGen holds operating licences and established community relationships across Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda, and Ethiopia, enabling rapid mobilisation without the country-entry delays that affect international contractors.

PowerGen is registered on the UN Global Marketplace (UNGM ID 263073) and is actively seeking to deepen its partnership with UNDP country offices across East Africa to support Sustainable Development Goal 7 (affordable and clean energy) and SDG 13 (climate action) programming. The company is available for RFPs, RFQs, and Long-Term Agreement frameworks covering mini-grid EPC, renewable energy consulting, project development services, and O&M contracts.

organization_profile_notes: LEGAL NAME: Enter 'POWERGEN RENEWABLE ENERGY EAST AFRICA LIMITED' exactly as it appears on the Kenya Certificate of Incorporation — no abbreviations, no trading names. UNGM and UNDP eTendering must match character-for-character.
UNGM ID: Enter 263073 in the UNDP eTendering profile's UNGM reference field. This links the two records and allows UNDP to auto-import your UNGM data.

UNSPSC CODES — RECOMMENDED SET (verify at https://www.unspsc.org before submission): 26111700 (Photovoltaic cells and modules), 26111701 (Solar photovoltaic panels), 26111800 (Power storage systems — batteries), 81101500 (Engineering and design services), 72101500 (Building construction and support), 76111500 (Power generation services), 81141600 (Project management), 77101500 (Environmental servi
COMPANY TYPE: Select 'Private Company / Limited Liability' or equivalent. Do NOT select 'NGO' or 'Government' — PowerGen is a commercial EPC contractor.

COUNTRY OF REGISTRATION: Kenya. Enter Nairobi as the primary address. List Tanzania (Arusha), Uganda (Kampala) as secondary operational addresses in the 'additional locations' or 'countries of operation' fields.

FINANCIAL CAPACITY: UNDP eTendering may ask for annual turnover ranges. Use the Deloitte 2024 consolidated audit figures. If the portal asks for a single-year figure, use the most recent (2024) audited revenue. Do not use projected or unaudited figures.

AUDITED FINANCIALS FORMAT: Upload as a single combined PDF (all three years — 2022, 2023, 2024) if the portal allows multi-year uploads in one file. If separate uploads are required, label each file by year. Deloitte letterhead and signature page must be visible.

REFERENCES: UNDP eTendering typically has a structured 'past performance' or 'references' section. Enter the USAID Power Africa contract as Reference 1 (client: USAID/Power Africa; contract value: enter if available; period: 2019-2024; description: multi-year mini-grid grant execution, 40+ mini-grids, Kenya). Enter AfDB SEFA as Reference 2. Add Shell Foundation as Reference 3 if a field is availab

ISO CERTIFICATIONS: Upload the combined ISO 9001 + ISO 45001 certificate PDF. In the certification fields, enter the certifying body name, certificate number, and expiry date exactly as printed on the certificate.

INSURANCE: Enter the Professional Indemnity insurance details (insurer name, policy number, coverage amount, expiry date) in the insurance fields. Note: UNDP may also require public liability / third-party liability insurance for works contracts — check whether PowerGen holds this and add if available.
LANGUAGES: Select English as the primary business language. Swahili may be listed as an operational language if the portal allows multiple entries.
NCAGE / NATO CODE: Not required for UNDP. Leave blank if prompted — this field is relevant only for NATO/defence procurement.
DUNS / LEI: UNDP eTendering does not mandate a DUNS number, but if PowerGen has one, enter it — it speeds up due-diligence checks. If not, leave blank.
DOCUMENT FILE SIZE: UNDP eTendering and UNGM both enforce a 5 MB per-file limit. The Deloitte 2022-2024 combined financials PDF may exceed this — compress or split by year if needed.
output.cover_letter_draft:
Dear UNDP Procurement Team,

POWERGEN RENEWABLE ENERGY EAST AFRICA LIMITED (UNGM ID: 263073) respectfully submits this vendor registration package for inclusion on the UNDP supplier roster, with particular relevance to energy access, climate action, and rural infrastructure programming across East Africa. Founded in 2011 and headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, PowerGen is a specialist solar PV and battery storage mini-grid developer and EPC contractor with a proven track record of delivering over 60 operational mini-grids serving more than 45,000 households across Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda, and Ethiopia. Our work has been funded and validated by USAID Power Africa, the African Development Bank's Sustainable Energy Fund for Africa, and the Shell Foundation, and our financial statements have received a clean audit opinion from Deloitte East Africa for three consecutive years (2022–2024).

PowerGen is ISO 9001 and ISO 45001 certified, operates in-country teams across five East African markets, and has the regulatory licences, community relationships, and field execution capacity to mobilise rapidly in support of UNDP country office programming under SDG 7 (affordable and clean energy) and SDG 13 (climate action). We are committed to the principles of the UN Supplier Code of Conduct and attach our Code of Conduct and Anti-Corruption Policy as evidence of our governance standards. We welcome the opportunity to support UNDP's development mandate and are available to respond to RFPs, RFQs, and Long-Term Agreement frameworks at short notice. All supporting documents are enclosed in accordance with UNDP eTendering requirements.
submission_guidance: PORTAL NAVIGATION: Go to https://procurement-notices.undp.org. Click 'Supplier Registration' or 'Create Account' — do not confuse this with the UNGM registration portal. These are two separate systems; both must be completed.

UNGM LINK: During UNDP eTendering registration, you will be asked for your UNGM ID. Enter 263073. This triggers an automatic data pull from UNGM — verify that the imported data (legal name, address, UNSPSC codes) is correct before finalising.

COUNTRY OFFICE REGISTRATION: UNDP procurement is decentralised. After creating your global account, navigate to each country office section (Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda, Ethiopia) and register your interest / subscribe to tenders for each. Failure to do this means you will not receive notifications from country offices even if your global profile is complete.
TENDER SEARCH: Use the 'Search Tenders' function and filter by: Country = Kenya / Tanzania / Uganda / Rwanda / Ethiopia; Category = Energy, Environment, Infrastructure. Save these searches as alerts.

RESPONSE WINDOW: Most UNDP RFPs and RFQs have a 2-3 week response window. Do not wait for a tender to appear before preparing your bid library. Have the capability statement, financials, ISO certs, references, and insurance certificate in a single ready-to-attach folder.

COMMON REJECTION REASONS: (1) Legal name mismatch between UNGM and UNDP eTendering — use the exact name from the Certificate of Incorporation on every document. (2) Expired documents — check ISO certificate and insurance expiry dates before submission. (3) Overly broad UNSPSC codes — UNDP buyers filter by specific codes; if your codes are too high-level, your profile will not surface. (4) Missing tax registration certificate — this is a common gap for East African vendors; obtain the Kenya PIN certificate before submitting. (5) Uncompressed PDFs exceeding 5 MB — compress large files before upload.

CODE OF CONDUCT: The PowerGen Code of Conduct + Anti-Corruption 2024 is currently a .docx file. Convert it to PDF before uploading — UNDP portals typically do not accept .docx for compliance documents.

FINANCIAL STATEMENTS: If the Deloitte 2022-2024 combined PDF exceeds 5 MB, split into three separate annual files: 03a_Audited_Financials_2022.pdf, 03b_Audited_Financials_2023.pdf, 03c_Audited_Financials_2024.pdf.

FOLLOW-UP: After submitting, email the procurement focal point at each UNDP country office (Kenya: procurement.ke@undp.org; Tanzania: procurement.tz@undp.org — verify current addresses on the UNDP country office websites) to introduce PowerGen and flag your registration. Relationship-building at the country office level significantly increases the likelihood of receiving direct RFQ invitations.

PROFILE REFRESH: UNDP eTendering profiles can become stale. Set a 6-month calendar reminder to log in, update any changed documents, and confirm that your UNSPSC codes still reflect your active service lines.
